feature.title: R1: block-level miss predictor and capped read policy, offline (Track B round 2)

brief.goal: On the existing B0 corpus, find out whether a learned predictor gives a better **feasible** speculative read policy than the native gate (with and without floors) at L+1, under a per-layer read cap and a mean read budget, with the complete offline scorer cost and a timing-sensitivity replay measured. The answer is a dev/calib result labelled "exploratory on reused data; independent confirmation pending", not a serving change.
criteria: A frozen, hashed `run_plan.json` exists in the new run directory before any training stage runs, and names every arm, parent, seed, epoch limit, objective, selection metric, calibration rule and the continuation gate.

Stage 1 (no training) reports, on dev and calib, for F0 (the frozen B1 head `h1_E5_r128_h512_w2.0.pt`), bare gate, gate + floors and the gate-rank/learned-admission hybrid: useful / wasted / eligible rows, precision, recall, total reads, under cap 1 and cap 2 at mean reads <= 1 per forward-layer, plus the per-forward-layer read histogram (0/1/2/3/4+ before capping, p50-p99, max) by layer, stratum and session.
Stage 1 also reports a timing-sensitivity replay (zero / nominal / adverse drive contention, scorer delay included) that prices on-time useful rows, not every useful row at the last-miss slope.

Training arms T0-T4 (and T5/G0 only if Stage 2 runs to them) are trained on train, selected on dev by the capped-policy metric, and thresholded on calib; each arm's curves, checkpoint hashes and parent hashes are saved.

One shared group-level scoring path scores every control and candidate with identical groups, skip masks and eligible denominators (a test asserts it), and no pooled score goes through noisy-or a second time.

The complete offline scorer cost (gate scores, feature build, head, block aggregation, hot/RAM filtering, threshold and cap selection) is measured under a CUDA graph at 6 live tokens, beside head-only cost.

`REPORT.md` and `results.json` in the run directory state the continuation-gate outcome, and say which of ranking, abstention, block aggregation, capacity, training length or lead explains any gain, and which remain unresolved.
The historical B1 run directory, its selection file and its verdict are untouched, and the old locked-test shards are never loaded.

R1: Follow `.claude/rules/divix01-run-protocol.md`: push, then a private divix01 worktree; `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python`; CPU under `taskset -c 0-63` with `OMP_NUM_THREADS`; GPU under `flock /data/models/slang/nvfp4-work/cc-gpu.lock taskset -c 32-63`; lock order disk then GPU; read PIPESTATUS.

Layout: new flat modules `analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/r1_*.py`, each with its test beside it as `test_r1_*.py`, mirroring the b1_*/test_b1_* pairs. The driver is `r1_run.py`. Do not edit `b1_*.py` unless a task explicitly owns an additive symbol there.

Module header copies `b1_score.py`: a docstring stating purpose, inputs and a Usage line; `HERE`/`REPO`; `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` for `scripts/dsv41`, `analysis/dsv41-drive/router-capture` and `HERE`; sibling imports with `# noqa: E402`, then sglang imports (e.g. `from sglang.srt.layers.moe.ram_slot_map import LaneKind`).

Reuse, don't reimplement: `b1_rows.Group`, `read_groups`, `read_x`, `x_rows`, `eligible`, `in_ram`; the RAM-snapshot + hot skip semantics of `b1_score._skip_mask`; `b1_baselines.GateScorer` and `load_floors` for the native controls; `b1_head.load_head`, `B1Head`, `make_batch`, `fit_train_pca_from_shards` for F0/T0; `llapor.MiddlePredictor` and `llapor.encode_features`; `b0_integrity._gates` for target gate weights; `residency_capture.load_residency` (`snap_stamp`, `label_stamp`, `keys`) for timing. Never modify `llapor.py`, `b0_*.py`, `residency_capture*.py`, `router_score.py`, `tier_sim.py` or the B0/B1 on-disk formats.

Miss kinds come from `LaneKind.MISS_GPU` (4) and `LaneKind.MISS_CPU` (5) imported, never literals; `HIT_SM` (2) is not a miss, kind 0 is VRAM hot (`KIND_VRAM_HOT`). Eligible rows are unique per (forward, target layer, expert).

Gate math is fp32 `sqrt(softplus(x @ W[row].T)) + bias[row]` with x decoded by `router_score.bf16_to_f32`; margins are to the token's 6th score (index 5). Every ranking breaks ties by ascending expert id (`np.lexsort((ids, -vals))` / stable argsort), as `b1_score._candidate_arrays` does.

The R1 group-score contract returns one block score per expert per group (f32 [384], -inf = not a candidate); it is consumed directly by the policy and is never routed through `b1_score._aggregate`'s noisy-or. Token-score controls (max, noisy-or) are pooled exactly once, in the R1 pooling helper.

Data containers are `msgspec.Struct` (frozen where possible), never `@dataclass`. Pure functions, called by keyword when they take 2+ args; functions under ~100 LOC; no defensive getattr/hasattr; protected `_name` helpers unless callers need them.
Comments: ASCII, one or two lines, only facts the code cannot show (units, layouts, the source of a constant such as a section-33.24 cost). No Args/Returns blocks on internal helpers.
Determinism: every source of randomness (init, epoch shuffles, subsampling, bootstrap) takes an explicit seed; seeded CPU runs give identical results.

Tests are CPU-only and synthetic (small hand-built Groups in `tmp_path`, following `test_b1_rows._group`) unless they need CUDA. GPU tests use `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs CUDA")`. The real-data smoke is opt-in via env vars (`SGLANG_R1_DATASET`, `SGLANG_R1_MODEL`, `SGLANG_R1_CORPUS`), as `test_b1_run.py` does with `SGLANG_B1_*`. No `pytest.main()` blocks.

Checks: laptop-side only `python3 -m py_compile <files>`; pytest only through `/Users/dnikolaidis/.hx/checks/divix01-pytest` with named files (`--gpu -s` for CUDA). Never write uv, pip or `.venv/bin/python` into a check, and never commit `python/uv.lock` or `python/.python-version`.

Driver: argparse `main(argv) -> int` with named stages (plan, audit, stage1, train arms, seeds, l2, calib, cost, replay, report). Each stage writes `stages/<name>/DONE.json` atomically (write tmp, then `os.replace`) with input and output sha256s; a stage reruns or refuses when its recorded inputs no longer match. The driver refuses any `--out` outside `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/` or equal to `b1-run-20261012`, and records every invocation with its exit code.

Workers never run the full study. The real run is a final owner-started task; documents record its numbers as `pending`. DSV41_REFERENCE gets a new `### 33.27` after section 33.26 and before `## Sources`, in 33.26's style (intro, paths, rerun block, test commands); section 33.26 and the B1 verdict stay unchanged.

Frozen constants (D16, D17) live in one place, `r1_plan.default_plan`, with their source cited in a one-line comment: contention {zero: 1.0, nominal: 2.0, adverse: 3.0} (DSV41_REFERENCE section 33.16), cost dtype 'bf16 head+aggregator, fp32 gate' with an fp32 reference. r1_timing and r1_cost read them from the plan and never hard-code their own.

The detailed design is `RAM_PREFETCH_B1_RESULTS_HANDOFF.md` section "DESIGN CRITIQUE - round 1" (R1.1-R1.11), as amended by the Decisions above. Where they differ, the Decisions win.

### Data and groups
A new R1 reader over the B1 dataset yields whole groups (session, block, forward, source layer, horizon) with tokens, live mask, position index, source features, target gate top-12, target ids/kinds, hot set and RAM snapshot, applying the exclusion manifest. Labels: `route_y[g,m,e]` per live token, `miss_y[g,e]` as a union, `available[g,e]`. Report both the historical-compatible denominator (all true misses) and the addressable subset. A device cache keeps groups contiguous so batches are whole groups. Arms that need full 384 gate scores recompute them from source x and the frozen target gate weights and bias (`sqrt(softplus(x W^T)) + bias`), with a top-12 parity check against the stored features. T5/G0 stream raw bf16 x (train ~9.2 GB) rather than cached PCA features.

### Models
The B1 E5 token encoder (rank 128, hidden 512, 16-wide layer and stratum embeddings) is the base. Block aggregator: per expert, anchor score and present flag, max draft score and present flag, max, mean, std, sum, noisy-or, live count, plus target-layer and stratum embeddings, into a shared Linear-GELU-Linear MLP of width 32 giving one block logit per expert. Position arm: 8-wide embedding of position 0-5 and a live-width scalar. Adapter arm: `z = W v + U[t] V[t] v + b[t]`, V [16,512], U [384,16], U and b zero-initialised. G0: `z = a[t] * s_native + b[t] + B[t] GELU(A x + pos)`, `s_native` the full 384 biased early margins to the 6th, A [64,5120], B [384,64] zero-initialised, a=1.

### Read policy and metrics
Per group: block scores for all experts, remove hot, snapshot-RAM and in-flight rows (same definitions for every policy), keep scores above the global threshold, rank, tie-break by expert id, truncate to cap 1 or 2. Metrics per policy: useful, wasted, eligible, precision, recall, outside-top-12 recovery, whole-layer coverage, read histogram and burst lengths, per-position and anchor-only/draft-only/shared row-set attribution, MISS_GPU/MISS_CPU split, warm-start and flagged subsets, block-level reliability bins.

### Timing sensitivity and cost
Join B0 snapshot and demand stamps by block/seq/layer to get each forward-layer's prediction-to-demand window; admit reads in score order while the modelled per-layer window (row read time from measured costs, contention multiplier 1 / nominal / adverse) and the scorer delay allow; count a read on time only if it lands before demand, and price remaining stall only for partial arrivals. Report assumptions beside results. Cost: CUDA graph at 6 live tokens of gate scores, feature build, head, aggregation, filter and selection, at the intended dtype; head-only beside it; parameter and buffer bytes.

### Driver and outputs
A new resumable R1 driver with named stages (plan, audit, stage1, train arms, seeds, l2, calib, cost, replay, report), each writing an atomic DONE record with input/output hashes; a stage resumes only when its inputs match. Outputs in the run directory: `run_plan.json`, exclusion and input manifests, per-arm configs and hashes, curves, seed comparisons, per-group read records for dev/calib, policy curves, calibration tables, replay assumptions and results, cost, `selection.json`, `REPORT.md`, `results.json`, and every invocation with its exit code.

# R1: block-level miss predictor and capped read policy, offline (Track B round 2)

## Goal
On the existing B0 corpus, find out whether a learned predictor gives a better **feasible** speculative read policy
than the native gate (with and without floors) at L+1, under a per-layer read cap and a mean read budget, with the
complete offline scorer cost and a timing-sensitivity replay measured. The answer is a dev/calib result labelled
"exploratory on reused data; independent confirmation pending", not a serving change.

## Acceptance criteria
- A frozen, hashed `run_plan.json` exists in the new run directory before any training stage runs, and names every arm, parent, seed, epoch limit, objective, selection metric, calibration rule and the continuation gate.
- Stage 1 (no training) reports, on dev and calib, for F0 (the frozen B1 head `h1_E5_r128_h512_w2.0.pt`), bare gate, gate + floors and the gate-rank/learned-admission hybrid: useful / wasted / eligible rows, precision, recall, total reads, under cap 1 and cap 2 at mean reads <= 1 per forward-layer, plus the per-forward-layer read histogram (0/1/2/3/4+ before capping, p50-p99, max) by layer, stratum and session.
- Stage 1 also reports a timing-sensitivity replay (zero / nominal / adverse drive contention, scorer delay included) that prices on-time useful rows, not every useful row at the last-miss slope.
- Training arms T0-T4 (and T5/G0 only if Stage 2 runs to them) are trained on train, selected on dev by the capped-policy metric, and thresholded on calib; each arm's curves, checkpoint hashes and parent hashes are saved.
- One shared group-level scoring path scores every control and candidate with identical groups, skip masks and eligible denominators (a test asserts it), and no pooled score goes through noisy-or a second time.
- The complete offline scorer cost (gate scores, feature build, head, block aggregation, hot/RAM filtering, threshold and cap selection) is measured under a CUDA graph at 6 live tokens, beside head-only cost.
- `REPORT.md` and `results.json` in the run directory state the continuation-gate outcome, and say which of ranking, abstention, block aggregation, capacity, training length or lead explains any gain, and which remain unresolved.
- The historical B1 run directory, its selection file and its verdict are untouched, and the old locked-test shards are never loaded.

## Decisions
- Offline only. No serving code, no capture, no A/B, no production change in this feature. Any serving design is a later hx feature.
- Reuse the corpus `b0-corpus-100-20261012`, the dataset `b1-dataset-20261012` and the 60/15/10/15 session split. The old locked test counts as already observed: its raw shards are never loaded; its saved tables may be quoted as historical.
- Staged with a stop: Stage 1 (F0 and native controls under caps, histograms, timing sensitivity) runs first because it tests the decisive unknown (does the thresholded advantage survive caps and timing) at no training cost. Stage 2 (training) runs automatically only if, on dev under cap 2 at mean reads <= 1, F0's recall beats the best native control by >= 10% relative and its on-time useful rows stay above that control's under nominal contention. Otherwise the run stops after Stage 1 and reports.
- The primary objective is block-level: `miss_y[g,e]` = some live token routes e as MISS_GPU or MISS_CPU, masked by `available` (not VRAM-hot, not RAM-resident at prediction); per-group BCE averaged over available experts, then over groups. Auxiliary token route BCE at weight 0.25 in joint arms. (Note: on available experts a route is a miss up to the 0.56% eviction rate, so the expected gain is from union labels and abstention, not from a label mismatch.)
- Arm ladder at L+1, sequential, each from its parent's copied checkpoint: F0 frozen B1 head; T0 same E5 architecture and original loss, up to 60 epochs; T1 frozen T0 encoder + learned block aggregator (block BCE); T2 unfreeze encoder, block BCE + 0.25 route BCE; T3 + position embedding (8-wide, positions 0-5) and live width; T4 + rank-16 target-layer residual output adapters (U, b zero-initialised). T5 (trainable 128-wide projection initialised from PCA, lr x0.1) and G0 (full 384-score native-margin residual challenger, rank 64) only after T4, as one further stage. If an arm adds nothing, the next arm builds on its parent.
- Controls kept in every table: bare gate, gate + floors, max-pooling and noisy-or pooling over the same token scores, and the hybrid (native gate's top available row, admitted only when the learned block score clears the cut). prev and pop are sanity rows only.
- Training recipe: AdamW, new parameters lr 1e-3, inherited 1e-4, weight decay 1e-2, dropout 0.1; warmup then cosine; 512 whole groups per optimizer step (gradient accumulation if memory demands); early stop after 8 epochs without improvement; seed 0 for screening; seeds 1 and 2 for T0 and the selected candidate's full ancestry; selection by median dev score across seeds, the seed-0 checkpoint is the candidate.
- Selection metric (dev): best eligible-row recall along an exact sorted-threshold sweep under cap 2 with mean reads <= 1 per forward-layer; ties to lower scorer cost, then fewer parameters. Cap 1 reported as its own lane, never used to veto or rescue cap 2.
- Calibration (calib, after selection): one global threshold per model and horizon for the capped policy; the lowest threshold within mean reads <= 1 on calib, equal-read ties toward the higher threshold.
- Continuation gate (frozen in run_plan.json; it does not rewrite B2): under cap 2 the candidate's recall is >= 10% relative above the best native control at the same budget; at the calib operating points no lower precision and no more than 5% extra reads; complete scorer median <= 0.1 ms per layer; the advantage holds across seeds, without flagged sessions, and under the timing sensitivity model's nominal case.
- L+2: after L+1 selection, train the selected architecture and its matched control at L+2 with the same recipe and budget. L+4 only if L+2 shows useful extra lead. Horizons are not combined in this feature.
- Timing replay is a bounded sensitivity model built from B0's per-forward residency/demand stamps and measured row-read costs, with zero/nominal/adverse contention and the measured scorer delay. It is labelled a model. No new trace infrastructure.
- The scorer-cost measurement covers what can be reproduced offline (gate scores through candidate selection). Publication to the speculative readers and side-stream joins belong to the serving spec.
- The one non-tie capture mismatch (b000 seq 1283, layer 39, token 1) is excluded through an explicit exclusion manifest applied by the R1 reader to every arm and control, with its affected source and target groups listed.
- Bootstrap estimand, for any later confirmation: paired whole-session resampling, 10,000 resamples, seed 0, pooled recall difference (candidate minus control) under the chosen capped policy. In this feature it is reported on dev as exploratory.

## Rules
- Follow `.claude/rules/divix01-run-protocol.md`: push, then a private divix01 worktree; `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python`; CPU under `taskset -c 0-63` with `OMP_NUM_THREADS`; GPU under `flock /data/models/slang/nvfp4-work/cc-gpu.lock taskset -c 32-63`; lock order disk then GPU; read PIPESTATUS.
- Production on divix01 is stopped: never start, stop or restart it; never touch `cc-expert-prediction/dsv41-direct-prod`.
- Outputs only under `/mnt/nvme1/nvfp4-work/` in a new `b1-r1-<date>` directory; never nvme0/2/4, never the B1 run directory.
- Never load `locked_test` shards. A reader asked for that split raises.
- Fits (PCA, normalisers, priors) use train only; selection uses dev only; thresholds use calib only.
- No future demand, acceptance, session name, group id or drive flag reaches a predictor input. Labels only.
- Padding never contributes to a loss, pooling, normaliser or metric. Group batches never mix tokens of different forwards.
- Keep the B1 code path reproducible: new R1 modules and a new driver; B1 modules change only where an addition is needed, with their existing tests still passing.
- Tests run through `~/.hx/checks/divix01-pytest [--gpu] <named files> -q -p no:randomly`; run only the affected files.
- Agents use opus or sonnet only.

## Non-goals
- No serving integration, new capture, confirmation capture or served A/B.
- No predictor for the DSpark draft stages' own 128-expert MoEs.
- No combined multi-horizon read policy.
- No per-layer or per-position thresholds in the first screen.
- No attention block encoder, full mHC residual features or pre-attention prediction point (deferred, handoff R1.11).

It refuses locked_test with no override (R4, C8), drops the tokens in the exclusion manifest (D14), and derives the D4 labels per group: route_y, miss_y as a union over live tokens, available, and both denominators (all true misses, and the addressable subset). It also defines the shared group-score and batch contracts every later task codes against (C5, S§1.1). The offline in-flight set is empty and documented as such: with one horizon, each (forward, target layer) group has exactly one source.
tasks.produces: As K-T1 v2, plus: R1Group gains x_index: int64[n] (each kept token's row in the session's x shard) and r1_groups.x_rows(xmap, r: R1Group) -> f32[n, hidden]. When D14 drops a token from the middle of a group, r.g.x_offset (left as the unfiltered group's) no longer addresses contiguous rows, so every consumer that reads source x (r1_gate, r1_cache, T5/G0 streaming, gate parity) must use r1_groups.x_rows(xmap, r) or r.x_index, never b1_rows.x_rows(xmap, r.g). Groups left with no tokens after exclusion are dropped by the reader.

tasks.title: Full 384-score target gate recompute and top-12 parity
tasks.intent: New r1_gate.py recomputes the full early target-gate scores from source x and the frozen target gate in fp32, as sqrt(softplus(x W^T)) + bias. It also gives the native margins to the 6th score, which G0 and the cost path use. It checks top-12 parity against a Group's stored gate_ids and gate_scores within the tie convention (S§1.1, S§2).

tasks.title: Run plan: arm ladder, gates, frozen timing and dtype constants

tasks.title: Data audit: exclusion manifest and input manifest
tasks.intent: New r1_audit.py resolves the D14 bookkeeping gap. It finds the integrity report's non-tie mismatch cells (b000 seq 1283, layer 39, token 1), lists every affected source and target group in train, dev and calib, and writes the exclusion manifest that r1_groups.load_exclusions reads. tasks.title: Shared capped read policy: pooling, threshold, cap, exact sweep, calibration
tasks.intent: New r1_policy.py is the single policy every control and candidate goes through (C5, S§1.3). It pools token scores once (max or noisy-or) and removes skip-mask rows. It then applies the global threshold, ranks with ties broken by expert id, and truncates to cap 1 or 2. It runs the exact sorted-threshold sweep for the best recall at mean reads <= 1 per forward-layer (D8), and the calib threshold rule (D9).

tasks.intent: New r1_metrics.py turns policy reads into the C2 tables. It covers useful, wasted, eligible (all and addressable) rows, precision, recall, outside-top-12 recovery and whole-layer coverage, by pooled/noflag/warm/layer/stratum/session. tasks.intent: New r1_aggregator.py adds the S§1.2 block aggregator. Per expert it builds anchor and draft features with their present flags, plus max, mean, std, sum, noisy-or and live count, all over live positions only. tasks.title: Timing-sensitivity replay model
tasks.intent: New r1_timing.py is the D12/C3 sensitivity model. Each forward-layer admits its ordered reads while the stamp window minus the scorer delay leaves room for row-read time x contention. The contention values are the plan's frozen D16 multipliers (zero 1.0, nominal 2.0, adverse 3.0), read from r1_plan and never hard-coded. A read counts as on time only if it lands before demand. Only partial arrivals' remaining stall is priced, and the output is labelled a model with its assumptions.

tasks.intent: New r1_challengers.py adds the later D5 arms. T5 replaces the PCA with a trainable 128-wide projection initialised from it, keeps the train-only centering, trains at lr x0.1 and reads raw x. G0 computes z = a[t]*s_native + b[t] + B[t] GELU(A x + pos) with A [64,5120] and B [384,64]. Its initialisation (B=0, a=1, b=0) makes step 0 equal the native margins. tasks.title: Group-preserving training loop with capped-policy selection
tasks.intent: New r1_train.py trains one arm from an ArmSpec. It uses AdamW param groups, warmup then cosine, and steps of 512 whole groups with gradient accumulation. The objective follows the arm, and training stops early after 8 epochs without improvement. Each epoch is selected on the D8 dev metric via r1_policy, and curves, checkpoints and the parent sha are saved. T0 also keeps its best-at-one-read checkpoint (D7, C4).

It times the D17 intended path (fp32 gate scores, bf16 head and aggregator) and the full fp32 path beside it, each with head-only time, percentiles and bytes. The dtypes come from the plan's CostSpec. It reports the fraction of groups whose capped read set differs between bf16 and fp32, and checks the torch selection against r1_policy.select.

tasks.intent: New r1_stage1.py runs Stage 1 on dev and calib (C2, C3, D3). F0, the gate controls, the poolings, the hybrid, prev and pop all go through r1_policy at cap 1 and cap 2, with mean reads <= 1. Each result becomes an r1_metrics report and r1_timing cases built from the plan's D16 contention values. The stage evaluates stage2_gate and returns results in the report schema, plus read records.

Seeds 1 and 2 repeat T0 and the selected ancestry, and the candidate is chosen by the median dev score with seed 0 deployed (D7). It then runs L+2 for the selected architecture and its control (D11), calibrates on calib (D9), and records all hashes (C4).

tasks.title: r1_run.py driver: stage order, plan freeze, audit, cost, report, Stage-2 stop

It freezes run_plan.json (with D16/D17) before any training (C1) and stops after stage1 when the stage2 gate fails (D3). It guards the out root, logs invocations, and writes REPORT.md and results.json with the continuation gate (C7). An opt-in real-data smoke test runs every stage.

tasks.title: DSV41_REFERENCE §33.27 and the owner's rerun block
tasks.intent: Add `### 33.27` after §33.26 and before `## Sources`, in §33.26's style. It covers the R1 modules, inputs and paths, and the exclusion manifest. It records the frozen D16 contention multipliers (citing §33.16) and the D17 cost dtypes. It gives the staged rerun block with locks and cores per stage and the divix01-pytest commands. Results stay `pending` under the exploratory label, and §33.26 stays untouched.

tasks.title: R1 data inputs: group reader and labels, gate recompute, exclusion audit, stamp join
tasks.intent: Everything R1 reads from the B1 dataset and B0 corpus enters here: the R1Group/labels contract, the full-gate recompute with parity, the exclusion and input manifests built on both, and the timing windows. One reviewer holding the b1_rows/b1_extract/residency_capture formats checks all four.
tasks.focus: The locked_test guard must raise at the call and offer no frozen-sha escape (R4, C8). Labels: miss_y is a union deduplicated per (forward, target layer, expert). available must equal not(hot or RAM snapshot), exactly as b1_score._skip_mask computes it. eligible_all keeps snapshot-to-demand evictions and eligible_addr does not. LaneKind values are imported, never written as literals. D14 exclusion: the b000 seq 1283 L39 token 1 cell is removed from every affected source group at every horizon, and those groups are listed. The anchor stays at position 0 after filtering. Gate parity: check the tie handling at the 12th score and fp32 math. Stamps: %globaltimer units, the join key against residency `keys`, and inversions and missing joins counted rather than dropped. No label, session or flag field may reach a model input (R6).

tasks.title: Shared capped read policy and its metrics
tasks.intent: One contract runs group score -> candidates -> threshold + cap -> reads, and the tables and bootstrap are computed from it. C5's single scoring path and every Stage-1 number depend on these two modules agreeing.
tasks.focus: Each score is pooled exactly once, and noisy-or never runs on a pooled score (C5). Groups, skip masks and denominators must be identical across scorers, with a test that asserts it. Ties break by ascending id. The exact sweep must cover every distinct value, and mean reads must count zero-read groups. D8 (best under budget) and D9 (lowest feasible threshold, equal-read ties to the higher one) are separate rules. Check >= vs > at the threshold. Histograms are taken before the cap, and cap-dropped useful reads must be counted correctly. The anchor-only/draft-only/shared row sets must be mutually exclusive. The D15 bootstrap resamples whole sessions with the same indices for both arms, from summed counts.

tasks.title: R1 model family: block aggregator, encoder arms, challengers, group cache
tasks.intent: One model surface: the GroupBatch/ModelInput tensors the cache builds, the aggregator and losses over them, the E5-based R1Model with position and adapter arms, and the T5/G0 challengers that feed the same aggregator.
tasks.focus: Padding (R7): the aggregator features, both losses and the cache must ignore non-live slots, with a test that changes a padded token and expects no change. Batches hold whole groups only. Block BCE is the per-group mean over available experts, then the mean over groups; groups with no available expert add no term. Step 0 must reproduce the parent: adapter U=0, b=0; G0 B=0, a=1, b=0. from_parent must deep-copy, never alias. Param groups split into new 1e-3, inherited 1e-4 and projection x0.1, and T1 freezes the encoder and embeddings. The collate's E5 features must match b1_head.make_batch bit for bit. T5 centering uses train only. The raw-x memory budget must hold. save/load must round-trip with the parent sha.

tasks.title: Training, arm ladder, seeds, L+2 and complete scorer cost
tasks.intent: These tasks turn the model family into selected, calibrated and costed candidates: the training loop, the ladder, seed, L+2 and calibration stages, and the cost measurement that breaks selection ties and feeds the continuation gate.
tasks.focus: Selection uses dev only and thresholds use calib only (R5), and there is no locked_test path anywhere. The epoch metric is r1_policy's cap-2/mean<=1 sweep, and T0 also keeps its recall@1 checkpoint. Check: 512 whole groups per step, correct grad-accumulation scaling, warmup then cosine, patience 8. Check how 'adds nothing' is decided and how the ancestry is recorded. The candidate is the median over seeds 0/1/2 across the full ancestry, with seed 0 deployed. Every curve, sha and parent sha is saved (C4). Cost (D17): the complete path runs in one CUDA graph with no host sync. The bf16 head and aggregator path uses fp32 gate scores, takes its dtypes from CostSpec, and its median feeds the 0.1 ms gate. The fp32 path is timed beside it, and the read-set difference fraction is computed on identical inputs. select_torch must match r1_policy.select, ties included. The GPU test must really run.
